campbell.title: Campbell City Council — September 1, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered a resolution to authorize a funding agreement with the Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority under the state's Low Carbon Transit Operations Program, which would support a transit reliability and performance improvement project. The agenda also referenced pothole damage claims processes.
keyTopics: Resolution to authorize a funding agreement with VTA under the Low Carbon Transit Operations Program for a transit reliability and performance systems project
Pothole damage claims process

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — September 2, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council reviewed routine items like meeting minutes, vendor payments, and the Treasurer's Report, and considered draft responses to two county Civil Grand Jury reports on pothole claims processes and VTA's oversight of BART Silicon Valley Phase II. The Council also took up a transportation impact fee study contract, forming a committee to look at alternative policing services, the future of the Saratoga Blossom Festival, and the city's continued involvement in the Cities Association of Santa Clara County.
keyTopics: Draft responses to Civil Grand Jury reports on pothole damage claims and VTA's management of BART Silicon Valley Phase II
Support for AB 1761, a bill on data transparency for utility rate calculations
An $85,000 contract with Fehr and Peers for a Transportation Impact Fee study
Forming an Ad-Hoc Committee to review alternative policing services in Saratoga
The future of the Saratoga Blossom Festival and continued involvement in the Cities Association of Santa Clara County

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — September 8, 2026
los-altos.summary: The Los Altos City Council took up routine budget and contract matters, including updated employee pay schedules and additional funding for an electrical maintenance contractor, alongside several administrative and civic items. Council also considered renaming Lee Street to Tubman Street, reviewed a citizen initiative on zoning impacts, and discussed changes to the Environmental Commission and Volunteer Awards Committee.
keyTopics: Revised Fiscal Year 2026/27 pay schedules for city employee groups (LAMEA, POA, management, and confidential staff)
Amendment adding $250,000 to the maintenance agreement with Bear Electrical Solutions
Proposal to rename Lee Street to Tubman Street
Disbanding the joint Los Altos–Los Altos Hills Volunteer Awards Committee in favor of a Los Altos-only committee
Citizen initiative presentation on potential impacts to zoning, plus discussion of the Environmental Commission

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — September 1, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council met to approve routine meeting minutes and consider a handful of administrative items, including vacating a public service easement on Cerro Vista and setting up new preferential and time-limited parking rules. The council also considered hiring a consultant to help with an executive-level hiring process.
keyTopics: Vacating a public service easement at 15995 Cerro Vista
Establishing preferential and time-limited parking permits
Hiring a consultant to assist with an executive search or hiring process
Approval of minutes from several recent closed session and regular Town Council meetings

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — September 2, 2026
san-jose.summary: The Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole met to plan upcoming City Council schedules, canceling the September 8, 2026 meeting and reviewing the draft agenda for September 15, 2026. The committee also considered the City Clerk's public record log for late August and took up a study session on financing tools that could support economic development infrastructure projects.
keyTopics: Cancellation of the September 8, 2026 Council meeting
Review and possible additions to the September 15, 2026 draft agenda
Public record log covering August 20–27, 2026
Study session on infrastructure financing tools for economic development

mountain-view.title: Mountain View City Council — September 8, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The Mountain View City Council began with a closed session to discuss performance evaluations for two top staff positions, the City Clerk and City Manager, as well as related labor negotiation matters. The regular public session that followed included a proclamation recognizing National Hispanic Heritage Month.
keyTopics: Closed-session performance evaluation of the City Clerk and City Manager
Labor negotiations discussion involving the City Clerk and City Manager as unrepresented employees
Proclamation recognizing National Hispanic Heritage Month

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — August 25, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The Sunnyvale City Council held a special meeting on August 25, 2026, beginning with a closed session followed by a public presentation. The presentation portion covered an update on the CleanWater Program.
keyTopics: Closed session held during the special afternoon meeting
CleanWater Program update presentation

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — September 1, 2026
cupertino.summary: This Cupertino City Council meeting was largely ceremonial, featuring several recognitions rather than major policy decisions. The Council honored a local resident's 100th birthday and highlighted awareness months, along with recognizing city staff in the Innovation & Technology Department.
keyTopics: Recognition of Bertha Smith's 100th birthday
Proclamation recognizing September as National Preparedness Month
Proclamation recognizing September 15–October 15 as National Hispanic Heritage Month
Recognition of the Innovation & Technology Department's Applications, GIS, Infrastructure, Multimedia, and Administration Divisions

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — August 25, 2026
santa-clara.summary: This Santa Clara City Council meeting was held in a hybrid format, allowing members of the public and one Councilmember to participate remotely via Zoom. The available agenda details primarily cover meeting logistics rather than substantive policy items.
keyTopics: Councilmember Chahal participated remotely from Panchkula, India
Meeting held in hybrid format with in-person and Zoom participation options for the public

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — September 1, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council, sitting as the Successor Agency to the former Redevelopment Agency, considered routine financial and administrative business tied to winding down old redevelopment obligations. This included confirming which city officials hold formal Successor Agency officer roles and authorizing the sale of refunding bonds to refinance existing redevelopment-era debt.
keyTopics: Confirming and designating city officials as officers of the Successor Agency to the Redevelopment Agency
Authorizing issuance and sale of 2026 Tax Allocation Refunding Bonds to refinance Successor Agency debt

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Climate Action and Sustainability Committee — September 4, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Climate Action and Sustainability Committee took a first look at the city's 2025 greenhouse gas inventory, including a broader look at so-called Scope 3 emissions (indirect emissions from things like purchased goods and commuting). The committee also reviewed different approaches the city could take toward its carbon neutrality goal and offered feedback on what staff should study further.
keyTopics: Preliminary review of the 2025 greenhouse gas inventory
Overview of Scope 3 emissions and what they include
Discussion of approaches to reaching the city's carbon neutrality goal
Committee feedback on areas for further staff analysis
Both items noted as not a project under CEQA
